raw_response:
# Android browser alternatives

**Vivaldi is the strongest match found for this particular problem.** Its Android help explicitly documents a reload button in the address bar, alongside swipe-to-refresh, and explains how to move the address bar to the bottom. That directly addresses the missing or inaccessible reload-control complaint. The official installation instructions describe a normal Google Play installation, and the browser exposes tracker/ad-blocking and privacy settings.

## Ranked candidates

### 1. Vivaldi for Android
Primary reference: https://help.vivaldi.com/android/android-appearance/android-vivaldi-mobile-interface/

Vivaldi can replace Firefox with a Play-installable browser whose documented Android address bar includes an explicit reload button and site-level tracker/ad-blocking controls. Its configurable tab bar and address-bar position could help make navigation comfortable. The interface is feature-rich, so its usability should be judged on the actual phone rather than assumed from the feature list. The current installation documentation requires Android 10 or newer. Review the blocking level and privacy settings during setup; the privacy documentation says page preloading is enabled by default.

Installation: https://help.vivaldi.com/android/android-install/android-install-and-update-vivaldi-mobile/
Privacy controls: https://help.vivaldi.com/android/android-privacy/privacy-and-security-settings-in-vivaldi-on-android/

The December 3, 2020 release announcement independently establishes earlier Android availability, a Google Play download, privacy features, and a reload menu control. It does not establish when the current address-bar layout appeared.
Dated source: https://vivaldi.com/blog/vivaldi-3-5-for-android/

### 2. Brave for Android — useful, but reload placement remains unverified
Primary reference: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en-US&id=com.brave.browser

Brave can cover the Google Play and built-in privacy-protection requirements, with an Android Chromium-based browser offering default ad and tracker blocking. The official listing confirms a ready-to-install app and describes tracking protection and private tabs. I did not obtain sufficient primary evidence for the location and ease of access of the current Android reload control, so this is a conditional alternative rather than a confirmed solution to the central interface complaint.

Its product includes optional AI, Rewards, and VPN features, which could affect whether the interface feels sufficiently simple. Its Play data-safety declaration also reports possible collection of several data categories; built-in tracker blocking should not be interpreted as a promise that the app never handles user data.

Official browser description: https://brave.com/about/

### 3. DuckDuckGo for Android — a privacy-oriented alternative with an unresolved reload check
Primary reference: https://duckduckgo.com/duckduckgo-help-pages/mobile/android

DuckDuckGo can address easy Play installation and integrated privacy protection, including tracker blocking, encrypted-connection upgrades, and a control for clearing browsing data. It is a plausible choice when reducing routine privacy configuration matters. However, I could not verify an accessible Android reload button from the opened primary material; attempted public source-code retrieval was blocked. I would not select it solely to fix the reload problem without inspecting that control first.

The Android implementation has documented platform-specific protection limits, so its protection set is not identical to its desktop browsers. The current Play listing also includes optional AI and subscription features; these are separate from the free browser's basic availability.

Play listing: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.duckduckgo.mobile.android
Protection details: https://duckduckgo.com/duckduckgo-help-pages/privacy/web-tracking-protections

### 4. Firefox Focus for Android — a different workflow for short private sessions
Primary reference: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/what-firefox-focus-android

Firefox Focus offers a separately installable, privacy-focused Android browser with tracking protection and an easily reached session-erasure control. Mozilla's dated support article confirms free Google Play availability and configurable content blocking. This provides an alternative mechanism: a simpler workflow centered on disposable browsing sessions.

It remains a Mozilla product, and the opened source did not establish the position or accessibility of its reload control. Its session-erasure emphasis may also be inconvenient for someone who wants persistent browsing state. It is therefore a weaker fit for a full replacement until the desired navigation and session behavior are checked.

## Evidence limits

The ranking reflects the stated requirements, with direct evidence for a reload control weighted heavily; it is not a hands-on usability or privacy audit. No browser was installed or tested. Vivaldi and Firefox Focus have opened dated material preceding the October 21, 2026 question date, while the current Vivaldi help layout itself is undated. Brave and DuckDuckGo's opened Play listings were updated November 19, 2026, so those listings are later evidence. Other live pages with no reliable version date are marked unknown.

An unauthenticated grep.app code-search request failed. Two code-through-web fallback queries were attempted, and subsequent GitHub/raw-source opens were blocked; this was not a successful native code search. The shortlist is deliberately limited to four candidates, with only Vivaldi directly substantiated against the reload requirement.
